title: How much time passed before and after recorded approval?
question: Which parts of the filing-to-issuance interval can be measured from the two building permit registers?
finding: Of 439,809 unique applications filed since 2012, 405,851 had a usable approval interval; 404,685 also had an issuance date on or after approval.
how: Match primary-address permit numbers to the all-address ledger’s distinct approval dates. An unambiguous calendar approval date on or after filing is required. For the post-approval interval, issuance must occur on or after approval. Approval dates after issuance are shown as reversed and excluded from the post-approval interval. A separate column measures filing to the last recorded terminal status for unissued applications closed or denied.
limits: Approval and issuance can occur on different days, and the public records do not assign intervening time to either the applicant or the City. A status date is the latest recorded administrative event. End-of-work completion is separate. The City issuance metric counts both endpoints; this screen uses subtraction and counts same-day events as zero elapsed days.
